source_user: Give one misleading intuition about quantization and correct it. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Misleading intuition: using fewer bits automatically makes the whole inference service faster. Correction: packed weights and fused scale application can reduce weight bytes and memory traffic in a supported low-bit GEMM, but dequantization, metadata, unsupported operators, or launch overhead may dominate. Boundary: the result is workload- and phase-dependent; decode may still be limited by KV-cache bandwidth or scheduling, and small shapes may lack an optimized kernel. Compare an identical reference and candidate over production-relevant prompt/output lengths and concurrency, reporting prefill/decode p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, memory high-water marks, quality, fallbacks, and errors.
risks: Bit width alone does not predict end-to-end latency or quality; tensor coverage, calibration, kernels, hardware, and phase matter.
Average gains can hide tail latency, KV-cache pressure, fallback execution, quality regressions, or failed requests.
evidence_required: Exact tensor precision map, calibration/outlier policy, accumulator, device, runtime, kernel coverage, and workload matrix.
Repeated matched quality, error/fallback, component-memory, prefill/decode tail-latency, and throughput measurements with variability.

source_user: Give one misleading intuition about quantization and correct it. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Misleading intuition: reducing weight precision by half necessarily halves total serving memory and improves throughput. Correction: packed weight codes and scales reduce only the covered weight component and may reduce GEMM bandwidth; activations, KV cache, workspace, metadata, and unquantized layers remain. Boundary: if KV-cache capacity or a fallback operator is the bottleneck, the end-to-end result may be negligible or negative. Freeze checkpoint, tensor coverage, calibration, kernels, and workload, then measure component memory, high-water mark, prefill/decode latency tails, throughput, quality, allocation failures, and fallbacks against a matched reference.
risks: Storage savings are not total-memory savings when KV cache, activations, workspace, or metadata dominate.
Quality and reliability can change with calibration, outliers, and partial tensor coverage.
evidence_required: Per-component memory inventory and exact precision/coverage, calibration, kernel, device, and workload specifications.
Repeated matched memory, phase-specific latency, throughput, quality, error, and fallback results across relevant batch and length cells.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for quantization. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Use one fixed checkpoint, tokenizer, device, driver/runtime, serving implementation, and deterministic evaluation set. Compare a full-precision reference with one quantized configuration whose tensor map, bit format, scale granularity, calibration data, accumulator precision, and outlier policy are recorded. Mechanism: packed low-bit weights with fused scaling can reduce weight loads in a supported GEMM. Randomize repeated trials over representative prompt lengths, generated lengths, batch/concurrency, and warm-up state; measure prefill and decode p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, component/high-water memory, quality, errors, and fallback counts. Boundary: do not generalize from one shape or device; unsupported kernels or KV-cache limits can reverse the result.
risks: A single benchmark cell can confound quantization with kernel, scheduler, cache, or workload effects.
Calibration may preserve average quality while harming particular slices or increasing failures.
evidence_required: Frozen reference/candidate configs, tensor precision map, calibration set, seeds, hardware/software versions, and workload matrix.
Repeated paired trials with confidence intervals or variability, quality slices, phase-separated latency, memory components, throughput, errors, and fallback telemetry.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for quantization. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Build a paired experiment with the same checkpoint, tokenizer, prompts, output policy, hardware, runtime, and concurrency. Vary only the quantization configuration: record which weights/activations/KV tensors are quantized, bit format, scale granularity, calibration/outlier handling, and accumulation precision. Mechanism: packed weights and fused dequantization can lower bytes fetched by matrix multiplication. Collect repeated steady-state prefill/decode latency tails, throughput, memory high-water mark by component, quality on an agreed suite, errors, and kernel fallbacks. Boundary: a low-bit weight result does not establish an end-to-end result if activation traffic, KV cache, unsupported layers, or small-batch launch overhead dominates; report each phase separately.
risks: Changing runtime or workload along with precision prevents causal attribution.
End-to-end throughput may improve while tail latency, quality, or failure rate worsens.
evidence_required: Configuration diff limited to quantization, exact tensor map, calibration policy, device/runtime/kernel versions, and workload cells.
Paired repetitions with latency distributions, throughput, per-component memory, quality slices, errors, and fallback counts.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for quantization. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Start with a frozen full-precision baseline and a quantized candidate produced from the same checkpoint. Document tensor coverage, bit type, scales/zero points, calibration and outlier treatment, accumulator, operator fallbacks, hardware, software, and warm-up. Mechanism: quantized packed weights can reduce memory bandwidth for supported GEMM operations, while wider accumulation limits numerical error. Use the same representative prompt/output distribution and randomized repeated trials across batch, concurrency, and sequence lengths; measure quality and failures as well as prefill/decode p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and component memory. Boundary: any conclusion is conditional on this device, kernel path, and workload, and cannot be inferred from model size alone.
risks: Kernel fallback or numerical changes may confound speed and quality conclusions.
Representative averages can miss long-tail requests and vulnerable quality slices.
evidence_required: Immutable baseline/candidate manifests, tensor and calibration details, fallback logs, workload sampling method, and environment versions.
Repeated distributional metrics, quality by slice, failure/error counts, memory high-water marks, and phase-specific performance.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for quantization. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Use a blocked, matched comparison: keep model weights, tokenizer, request traces, sampling settings, device, runtime, and scheduler fixed; change only the documented quantization map and calibration. Record bit width, group size, scales, outlier handling, accumulation, and all fallback operators. Mechanism: a supported fused low-bit matrix multiply can read fewer weight bytes and apply scales during accumulation. Run warm-up followed by randomized repetitions across prompt/output lengths, batch, and concurrency, measuring prefill and decode latency distributions, throughput, per-component memory high-water marks, quality, errors, and admission failures. Boundary: do not claim universal gains from this test—small shapes, unquantized KV cache, or memory/scheduler saturation may dominate.
risks: A fixed trace may omit workload cells where quantization behaves differently.
Memory or scheduler saturation can make a component-level gain irrelevant to service behavior.
evidence_required: Matched trace and configuration manifest, precision/coverage and calibration details, runtime/kernel/fallback logs.
Repeated results across length/concurrency cells including p95/p99, throughput, memory components, quality, and failures.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for quantization. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Define a reference checkpoint and one quantized build, and pre-register the claim and acceptance gates: quality non-inferiority, error rate, memory, and phase-specific latency/throughput. Hold tokenizer, prompts, output lengths, serving code, device, runtime, scheduler, and concurrency policy constant. Mechanism: packed weights plus fused scale handling can reduce weight bandwidth in compatible kernels. Record exact tensor coverage, calibration/outlier policy, accumulator, workspace, and fallback path; repeat randomized trials after warm-up over production-relevant shapes and lengths. Boundary: the experiment cannot attribute a gain to bit width if kernels, batch regime, or cache state differ, and weight quantization alone says little about KV-cache-limited decode.
risks: Uncontrolled cache state, scheduling, or output length can bias comparisons.
A mean speedup may violate tail-latency, quality, or reliability requirements.
evidence_required: Pre-registered acceptance criteria, immutable configs, calibration and tensor map, environment, and randomized workload design.
Paired repetitions with uncertainty, quality/error slices, p50/p95/p99 prefill/decode latency, throughput, memory, and fallback telemetry.

source_user: Write a concise runbook entry for an engineer investigating quantization. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Runbook: (1) freeze checkpoint, tokenizer, device, runtime, workload, and quality/reliability thresholds; (2) inventory precision by tensor, calibration/outlier policy, scales, accumulator, workspace, and operator fallbacks; (3) compare against a matched full-precision build after warm-up; (4) capture prefill/decode p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, component memory high-water marks, quality slices, errors, and fallbacks across relevant lengths and concurrency; (5) inspect traces for the limiting kernel or cache component before concluding. Mechanism: packed weights with fused scaling can reduce weight traffic in supported GEMM. Boundary: lower weight storage or a microbenchmark speedup does not imply faster decode when KV-cache bandwidth or unsupported shapes dominate. Roll back if quality or reliability gates fail.
risks: Misidentifying the bottleneck can lead to optimizing weight traffic while decode is KV-cache or scheduler bound.
Quantization can introduce silent quality regressions or fallback-induced tail failures.
evidence_required: Baseline/candidate manifests, tensor precision and calibration inventory, trace/fallback logs, and quality/reliability thresholds.
Matched repeated measurements by phase, length, and concurrency, including memory components and error counts.

source_user: Write a concise runbook entry for an engineer investigating quantization. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Runbook: record the exact model, quantized tensors, bit format, scales, calibration set, outlier policy, accumulator, device, runtime, and kernel coverage. Establish a matched full-precision baseline, warm up both paths, then test the production length/concurrency matrix with repeated requests. Report prefill and decode latency tails, throughput, per-component memory, quality, errors, and fallbacks; use traces to identify whether the bottleneck changed. Mechanism: packed low-bit weights can reduce bytes loaded by a supported matrix multiply. Boundary: unsupported operators, small matrix shapes, unquantized activations/KV cache, or dequantization overhead can erase the benefit. Do not promote the build without passing quality and reliability gates.
risks: A benchmark on one shape or device may not represent service behavior.
Average throughput can conceal p99 regressions, fallback work, or quality loss.
evidence_required: Complete quantization and environment inventory plus matched workload definition.
Repeated phase-specific performance, memory, quality, error, fallback, and tail-latency measurements with variability.

source_user: Write a concise runbook entry for an engineer investigating quantization. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Runbook: freeze the reference and candidate configurations, document tensor coverage, bit/scaling scheme, calibration and outlier handling, accumulation, kernels, and fallbacks, then warm up and run matched production-like requests. Measure prefill and decode p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, component memory high-water marks, quality slices, errors, and fallback counts over batch/concurrency and prompt/output lengths. Mechanism: packed weights and fused scaling may lower weight bandwidth for supported GEMM. Boundary: this does not establish a universal service improvement—decode may be KV-cache bound, and unsupported shapes or layers may fall back. Investigate traces and retain the quantized build only if predefined quality, reliability, and performance gates pass.
risks: Partial quantization and fallback paths can make the observed result differ from the nominal bit width.
Quality failures may be slice-specific and absent from aggregate scores.
evidence_required: Frozen configs, exact precision map, calibration data/policy, kernel/fallback trace, and workload matrix.
Repeated matched phase metrics, component memory, quality slices, errors, tails, and reliability-gate results.
